Provenance
Our Collegiate Arch motif is partly inspired by Take Ivy , the indispensable 1965 classic that defined a generation of style. Consisting of candid photos taken on Ivy League campuses, Take Ivy was an immediate sensation in its home country of Japan, invigorating nascent subcultures while serving as an indispensable historical record of midcentury American menswear. The book has been hailed by The New York Times as “a treasure of fashion insiders.” Our Collegiate Arch collection pays homage to the enduring influence of American campus style.

p-drakes-9524756218069.d:
A tweed blazer is one of those things you don’t know you need until you have one. It has that knack of being both rugged and refined, the kind of jacket you end up reaching for more than you ever expected.
Cut in Drake’s signature silhouette, it features a natural shoulder, subtle waist shaping, and a light construction that allows the jacket to move gracefully with the wearer.
Expertly tailored and fully canvassed with a hand-shaped chest, the jacket drapes naturally over the body, offering both shape and comfort. Hand-attached collars and sleeves provide a flexibility unmatched by machine construction, allowing the jacket to adapt seamlessly to the wearer, while a buggy lining ensures fluidity across the back and shoulders, and traditional lapels, with a wider profile and richer belly, reflect our time-honed house style.
Cut from 13.8oz Harris Tweed, woven by hand in the Outer Hebrides at one of the islands’ legendary mills, long regarded as the benchmark for authentic tweed.

The silhouette is deliberately boxy and relaxed, borrowing from the straightforward proportions of factory coats and workshop jackets, designed to layer easily and move without fuss.

The result is a working coat in spirit, but one that sits just as comfortably with tailoring as it does with denim.

p-kamakurashirts-9573198725347.d:
Inspired by 1940s American vintage Hawaiian shirts, this piece combines timeless resort style with the traditional Japanese art of natural indigo dyeing, a technique that has been practiced since the Edo period.
Each shirt is dyed using a natural fermentation process without any synthetic chemicals. The color is created solely through the fermentation of sukumo (composted Japanese indigo leaves) and natural wood ash lye, producing a rich, authentic indigo unlike any chemical dye.
Because no harsh chemicals are used, the fabric retains its original softness, offering a smooth, comfortable feel from the very first wear. Experience a unique fusion of Japanese craftsmanship and classic American style.
Material
* Rich, layered indigo with exceptional depth and a clear, luminous finish.
* Naturally dyed without chemicals, preserving the fabric's soft, supple texture.
* Highly breathable and absorbent, helping keep you cool and comfortable while also reducing static buildup.
Design
* A gently curved open collar and rounded chest pocket reinterpret the spirit of 1940s Hawaiian shirts with a modern touch.
* Slightly wider shoulders and lower armholes create a relaxed, effortless silhouette.

A special shirt filled with memories and stories
Reviving a selection from Kamakura Shirts’ 1990s archives, this shirt has been reinterpreted for today’s modern lifestyle and fashion sensibilities. About GIZA96
A type of Egyptian cotton, one of the world’s three great cottons. Among Giza cotton varieties (numbered in the order they were developed), GIZA96 is the newest extra-long staple strain.
Its fibers are rich in natural oils, giving the fabric a refined sheen and luxuriously smooth handfeel.
Origin
Produced in Nishiwaki City, Hyogo Prefecture, one of Japan’s leading cotton-weaving regions.
The fabric’s supple drape and graceful fall are achieved through the combination of skilled craftsmanship and a rich natural environment.
